newsitem.title: USA: Credit risk measures seen helping US regulators.
newsitem.headline: Credit risk measures seen helping US regulators.

text.p: Advances in measuring and managing credit risk may lead to better regulation of financial institutions, Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips said Thursday.

The Fed is already reviewing systems used internally by some major banks to quantify credit risk -- the possibility that an institution will suffer a loss due to a default or non-payment on a bond, loan or other instruments.

"At present, some institutions are making significant strides on a number of fronts to better quantify and manage credit risk," Phillips said in a speech at a conference here sponsored by the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago.
Phillips did not name any specific banks. J.P. Morgan & Co Inc recently unveiled a product called Creditmetrics to measure credit risk.
Using such products, banks can compare the amount of risk they have taken in lending to the amount of capital they have deployed and calculate a "credit-risk adjusted" return on the investment.

"Credit-risk adjusted returns to capital are being used to construct a portfolio management framework for credit risk which, in turn, is providing a proving ground for a myriad of new instruments such as credit derivatives," Phillips said.
"These efforts might eventually lead to supervisory regimes that are more sophisticated and compatible with market incentives and management practices than are currently available," she said.
The "ultimate goal" may be capital standards for banks that are tailored to fit the risks taken, instead of the current uniform capital standards for credit risk, Phillips said.
But the effort to quantify credit risk is still in its infancy and several hurdles remain, including the lack of necessary data used to create computer models of credit risk, she said.
